html:
David Ben-Gurion was the main founder of the State of Israel and its first prime minister. He read out its declaration of independence in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948.

Born David Grün in Russian Poland, he moved to Ottoman Palestine in 1906 as a young Labour Zionist and worked on farms, including near the early collective at Degania. He built the Histadrut labour federation and from 1935 led the Jewish Agency, the Jewish community's government in British Mandate Palestine.

He led Israel through the 1948 war, merged the armed groups into one army and pushed mass immigration, which doubled the population within a few years, including the Jews leaving Arab countries. For Palestinians the same war was the Nakba, when some 700,000 fled or were driven out.

He served as prime minister from 1948 to 1954 and again from 1955 to 1963, then retired to a kibbutz in the Negev desert.
sum: David Ben-Gurion was the main founder of the State of Israel and its first prime minister. He read out its declaration of independence in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948.
